question.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨0,\,t,\,2{t}^{2}⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨0,\,t,\,2{t}^{2}⟩\times ⟨0,\,1,\,4t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & t & 2{t}^{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 4t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}t & 2{t}^{2} \\ 1 & 4t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 2{t}^{2} \\ 0 & 4t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & t \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2{t}^{2},0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(t)}^{2}+{(2{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{4}+{t}^{2}}, \\  & =t\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(2{t}^{2})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =2{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
